## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Google_Drive
This is an MCP server provided by Drive API. The server provides tools for developers to build LLM applications on top of Drive.

10	## Core Doctrine (locked)
11	
12	RULE: THE PURPOSE OF THIS GUIDEBOOK IS TO GET PEOPLE TO ASK THE RIGHT QUESTIONS. This is the most important principle governing the entire project. The guidebook is not a prescription manual. It is not an authority on measurements. It does not dictate values that designers, policymakers, or practitioners must apply. It is a thinking tool that equips people to ask the right questions about how to design for accessibility depending on the circumstance. Measurements, ranges, and reference data exist to support this process — they serve the questions, not the other way around. Every item specification, every BPC synthesis, every piece of guidebook prose must be evaluated against this standard: does it help the reader ask better questions about this design element? Does it surface considerations they would not have encountered otherwise? Does it make them think more critically about the specific situation they face? When you know better, you do better. A designer who knows what questions to ask will produce a better outcome than one who does not — even without perfection, even without specialist input. The guidebook aims to raise the floor of understanding for everyone who touches the built environment.
13	DATE: 2026-04-24 23:38 — enshrined as foundational principle; governs all other rules
14	
15	RULE: Disability populations are not uniform. Every person within a population code has a unique experience and unique functional limitations, even where there is significant overlap with others who share the same condition. There are different ways to struggle with mobility, different ways to be blind, different ways to have MS, different ways to be autistic, different ways to have dementia, different ways to experience PTSD. There is no generic ideal for any population. Specifications provide ranges and starting points — not definitive answers. It is rare for a disability to be experienced in isolation; co-occurring conditions are the norm. Every item specification must acknowledge functional variability within the population and discuss how co-occurrence affects the design parameter, because that is the lived reality of the people the guidebook serves. Population codes are a high-level organizing principle: at Universal Mode they are comprehensive (mapping all considerations); at Population Mode they offer insight (what to think about for a known population); at Person Mode they step aside because a person is not defined by their disabilities — OT works bottom-up from functional impairments because everything must be uniquely tailored to the individual.
16	DATE: 2026-04-24 23:38
17	
18	RULE: Design Modes governs all specifications. Universal Mode = Universal Design / Code Compliance (population-agnostic, fixed values). Population Mode = Population-Informed Inclusive Design (ranges; median as default). Person Mode = Person-Specific Co-Design (OT assessment resolves position within the Population-Mode range). DAR mandatory at all modes.
19	DATE: Established — pre-session
20	
21	RULE: Evidence hierarchy is seven tiers, per governance/tier-system.md (OPERATIVE 2026-05-25, owner directive "t2>t3 this is enshrined"; DR-2026-05-29 ACCEPTED 2026-07-13). Tier 1 = primary research with intervention-level or biomechanical control (OT-prioritized, not OT-exclusive, per D-E); Co-1 = lived experience / participatory design (CRPD Art. 4.3, co-primary with Tier 1); Tier 2 = synthesis — (a) systematic reviews / meta-analyses AND (b) named-organisation evidence-based standards; Co-2 = OT professional body CPGs (co-primary with Tier 2); Tier 3 = lower-control primary clinical research + grey-literature primary research (supporting; rarely the sole basis — T3-alone never reaches `stated`, per the tier3-stated-threshold DR); Tiers 4–6 = the regulatory stratum (international standards, national frameworks, statutory codes) — walled off from best-practice anchoring; convergence-not-evidence. The evidence hierarchy determines what constitutes best practice. Where higher-tier evidence exists, it governs.
22	DATE: 2026-03-19 19:00; consolidated 2026-03-29; elevated to Core Doctrine 2026-04-24 23:46; reconciled to the canonical ladder 2026-07-13 (ratification record; this rule previously restated the superseded pre-2026-05-25 ordering)
23	
24	RULE: Best practice means the most accommodating, thoughtful, respectful, dignified, and usable condition achievable for the disabled person. Best practice is determined by the evidence hierarchy — Tier 1 primary research, Co-1 lived experience, Tier 2 synthesis (SR/MA + named-organisation evidence-based standards), Co-2 OT CPGs — not by code consensus. Codes are Tier 6: the compliance floor, not the aspiration. Code consensus across jurisdictions establishes what most codes agree on; it does not establish what is most accommodating or most dignified. A BPC best_practice_synthesis that derives its value solely from code consensus is a weak-band (○) best-practice claim — "best practice as currently known," valid only when flagged code-derived with the convergence-not-evidence caveat, and never rendered unflagged or above the weak band (amended 2026-07-21, owner directive, Option A; `decisions/DR-2026-07-21-evidence-architecture-option-a-execution.md`). An unflagged or full-strength code-consensus best-practice claim is in error. The test: does this specification provide the most accommodating, dignified, usable condition the evidence supports — or does it merely reflect what codes agree on?

84	**RULE: Never write the same fact into a second table. Point, do not copy.**
85	
86	> *"If you have reference identification in tables that allow them to be cross-referenced, then you
87	> don't need to duplicate anything from one table to the other aside from that reference identifier
88	> because you can point to it. I could literally have a thousand tables. So long as each table has a
89	> row with a column that shares the same reference identifier, then you can call up information from
90	> any one so long as you point to the correct table and column."*
91	>
92	> *"If a crossing row 'carries' its own reason, that introduces the possibility of error and drift
93	> because it implies the reason is being written across two or more tables. It is better to have a
94	> table cell point to another table cell than to rewrite."*
95	>
96	> *"A crossing row only takes its reference ID. If it is providing a reason, then that reason is
97	> specific to the new table."*

103	- **A parity check is not a fix.** It makes a dual home *survivable*, therefore permanent. Do not add
104	  parity checks, triggers or CHECK apparatus to police a copy — remove the copy. (`CLAUDE.md` §1
105	  already puts the burden of proof on apparatus. H03/H04 were deleted for this reason, not weakened.)

107	  append-only and replay from the baseline, so a DROP replaying before the INSERT that names it
108	  breaks `migration_reproducibility` — the trap migration 062 sprang. The available shape is
109	  **writer-retire, reader-retire, NULL forward**; the column stays as a tombstone. **Grep
110	  `scripts/migrations/data_*` for the column name before proposing any drop. That grep is the gate.**

117	> to another stage. We do not need an author name in a synthesis table when synthesizing information.
118	> We do not need an author name when writing a specification in a specification table. We do not need
119	> an author name when rendering in a render table. If we have the same reference ID, then we know

879	## Owner ruling 2026-09-13 — a code value confirmed by research is upgraded; the empty circle is for code WITHOUT research backing
880	
881	> **"Sometimes code standards come from T1. If a code standard is being confirmed as genuine best
882	> practice according to studies, then the code/regulatory input can be upgraded."**
883	>
884	> **"It is when a code/regulatory input does not have research backing that it gets the empty circle."**
885	
886	**What this settles.** It was put to the owner as one of three band questions raised by the
887	2026-09-13 design pass: what strength a cell carries when its *finding* is T1 but its only *value*
888	comes from a code. The answer is the upgrade route, and it is ruled — not the two-part rendering
889	that was also on the table.
890	
891	**WHAT IT EXTENDS, AND THE EXTENSION IS THE POINT.** `evidence-architecture.md`'s **G1** re-grains a
892	T4/T5 source out of NON-ANCHORING on exactly one trigger: *"its evidence basis is documented as
893	traceable to T1/T2 evidence, with that provenance recorded on the source record."* That is a
894	**genealogy** test — where the number came from. This ruling adds a second, independent route:
895	**confirmation** — a study finding the code's value sound, whether or not anyone can trace how the
896	committee reached it. The two are not the same test and the corpus already separates them:
897	**REF-00980** concludes *"changes to the technical requirements for ramp slope and length cannot be
898	recommended at this time."* It establishes nothing about ADA's provenance. Under G1 as written it
899	re-grains nothing. Under this ruling it upgrades the value it confirms.

900	
901	**And it makes the empty circle CONDITIONAL where it was automatic.** `tier-system.md` §5 maps T6
902	(code-floor) to `○` flatly, and §8's band table gives `○ Weak` to "T6 (code-floor)" with a cell whose
903	entire basis is T4–T6 taking `○` regardless. After this ruling `○` marks the **unbacked** case
904	specifically: a code or regulatory input with no research behind it. A code value a study has
905	confirmed is no longer `○` by virtue of being a code.
906	
907	**WHAT THE RULING DOES NOT SAY, recorded so nobody fills it in silently.** Three things.
908	(1) **Which band an upgraded value lands in** — the ruling says "upgraded", not "upgraded to ●". The
909	natural reading is that it takes the band of the confirming evidence, so a T1 confirmation yields
910	`●`; that is a reading, not the ruling, and it is the next thing to put to the owner.
911	(2) **Whether T4/T5 and T6 behave alike here.** The ruling says "code/regulatory input" without
912	distinguishing them, while existing doctrine splits them — `◐` for T4/T5 citations, `○` for T6.
913	(3) **What counts as confirmation.** REF-00980's non-recommendation of change is the clear case. A
914	study that merely *uses* a code value as its rig setting is not confirming it, and that distinction
915	is exactly what the `confirms` / `tested_at` edges of migration 075 exist to record.
916	
917	**Mechanism, so this is executable rather than aspirational.** The 075 design gives the row-level
918	vocabulary: a `confirms` edge from a finding row to the code figure it confirms is the upgrade
919	trigger; `tested_at` is not; `insufficient` is the opposite and remains an open band question. The
920	engine rule that reads those edges is not yet built, so **the upgrade is ruled and unexecuted** —
921	which is the state an empty table should be read as, per the 2026-09-11 entry above.
922	
923	CONDITION: Any session assigning a strength band to a determination whose value comes from a code or
924	regulatory source, or citing G1's traceability clause as the only re-graining route.
925	ACTION: Treat confirmation-by-study as a second re-graining route alongside documented traceability.
926	Read `○` as "no research backing", not as "is a code". Record the confirming relation on the row
927	rather than asserting the upgrade in prose. Do not assume which band an upgraded value takes — that
928	is unruled.
929	DATE: 2026-09-13 — owner ruling, quoted above.

985

987	> you looked at them, I think"**
988	>
989	> — put back to the owner because the phrase carries two opposite readings, and confirmed as: **the
990	> finding supplies no VALUE, but is real evidence.** The cell stays `pending` on value; the finding
991	> anchors the cell in DIRECTION, remains first-class R7 harm evidence, and is rendered in the book.
992	
993	**Why it was queried rather than recorded as first stated.** In the 075 vocabulary `insufficient` is
994	a RELATION, not a quality grade: it points from a finding row to *the baseline that finding says is
995	inadequate*. So an "insufficient finding" is a finding **that the code is insufficient** — not a
996	finding that is itself weak. Read the second way, the ruling would have discarded REF-00784's
997	*"Between 10% and 100% of users would not be able to maneuver in spaces that meet current
998	Accessibility Guidelines"* and REF-00971's *"None of the scooters tested were capable of completing
999	all manoeuvres within the space allowed by existing standards"* as log entries. Those are T1 and T3
1000	findings that the built environment FAILS people, which the research contract's R7 makes first-class
1001	evidence rather than a by-product, and which the mission — *"get people to ask the right
1002	questions"* — points directly at. The clarification preserves them.
1003	
1004	**What the ruling settles.** Such a finding cannot say what the right number IS, so it supplies no
1005	value and cannot move a cell off `pending` on value. It can and does establish that the existing
1006	value is wrong for these people, and that is rendered.

1008	**The three band questions raised by the 2026-09-13 design pass are now all closed:** a code value
1009	confirmed by research is upgraded and `○` marks unbacked code (entry above); a derived figure takes a

1011	`insufficient` finding supplies direction, not value (this entry).

1026	## Owner ruling 2026-09-13 — grey literature that states a code's value is regulatory stratum, not independent evidence
1027	
1028	> **"If T3-grey is the same value as T6, I think T3-grey is not T3 but T6"**
1029	
1030	**What it is really about, and it is not the marker.** `tier-system.md` §5 maps T3-grey and T6 to the
1031	SAME band — both `○`. So re-tiering such a source changes no marker. What it changes is the
1032	**stratum** it sits in and, decisively, **whether it counts as an independent root**. Two `○` sources
1033	stating the same number read as two sources converging; if one is echoing the other's code, they are
1034	one source counted twice. That is the laundering this project already names
1035	*convergence-not-evidence*, and it is the consequential half of this ruling.
1036	
1037	**Machinery that already exists, so this is not built from nothing.** `v_value_independence` counts
1038	`DISTINCT COALESCE(root_ref_id, root_id)` and admits only `root_type IN ('measurement_primary',
1039	'participatory_finding', 'derived_calculation')` — a row recorded as `committee_assertion` or
1040	`untraced` already corroborates nothing. `echo_of` and `root_id` carry the transmission chain, and
1041	`references/methodology/value-genealogy-worked-example-corridor-width.md` is the worked precedent
1042	(1800 mm's zero in-corpus roots against 2440/2400 mm's two independent roots).
1043	
1044	**THE GAP THIS RULING FILLS.** All of that machinery tests **recorded provenance** — what an extractor
1045	wrote down about where a figure came from. The ruling supplies a test for the case where provenance
1046	was never recorded: **value coincidence with a code**. Grey literature overwhelmingly repeats code
1047	values, and an unrecorded echo currently reads as independent corroboration.
1048	
1049	**THE FALSE POSITIVE, stated because the rule is stated as an identity.** Two genuinely independent
1050	measurements can land on the same number; a code value is often round and grey fieldwork often
1051	reports round numbers. A T3-grey field study that independently measured 1500 mm and a code that says
1052	1500 mm are convergence, not echo, and automatic re-tiering would erase a real corroboration — the
1053	opposite error to the one the ruling prevents, and the harder one to notice afterwards.
1054	**Recommended shape, for the owner to confirm or reject:** the coincidence raises a rebuttable
1055	presumption of echo — the source sits in the regulatory stratum and contributes no independent root
1056	UNLESS its own recorded provenance shows independent measurement (`root_type='measurement_primary'`
1057	with a root that is not the code). That keeps the ruling's force, costs nothing when provenance is
1058	absent, which is the common case, and does not silently delete a genuine second root.
1059	
1060	CONDITION: Any session tiering a grey source whose value matches a code, or counting independent
1061	roots for a parameter.
1062	ACTION: Do not count a grey source as an independent root on value agreement alone. Check its
1063	recorded provenance first; where none exists, treat it as regulatory stratum. Expect no marker change
1064	— both bands are `○` — and expect the change to show up in independence counts and
1065	`regulatory_stratum_only`, which is where it matters.
1066	DATE: 2026-09-13 — owner ruling, quoted above. The rebuttable-presumption shape is a proposal, not
1067	the ruling.

1075	## Owner ruling 2026-09-13 — the derived-figure weighting function: mean of band ordinals, ROUNDED DOWN
1076	
1077	> **"yeah round down"**
1078	
1079	Closing the function left open by the weighted-average ruling above. The band ordinals are the
1080	weights: `●`=3, `◐`=2, `○`=1; the derived figure's band is the **floor** of the mean across its
1081	inputs. Verified against the owner's own worked case and its neighbours:
1082	
1083	| inputs | mean | band |
1084	|---|---|---|
1085	| 2×T1 + 1×T4 — **the owner's example** | 2.667 | **◐** |
1086	| 3×T1 | 3.000 | ● |
1087	| 2×T1 + 1×T6 | 2.333 | ◐ |
1088	| 1×T1 + 2×T6 | 1.667 | ○ |
1089	| 99×T1 + 1×T4 | 2.990 | ◐ |
1090	
1091	**The property that follows from `floor`, recorded so it is a decision and not a surprise.** Only an
1092	all-`●` input set reaches exactly 3.0, so **a single sub-`●` input caps the result below full circle
1093	at any scale** — the last row above. The rule is therefore equivalent to: *a derived figure is fully
1094	anchored only if every input is fully anchored.* That is consistent with the ruling it completes (the
1095	T4 costs you the full circle), and it is the strongest consequence of rounding down rather than to
1096	nearest.
1097	
1098	**What "weighted" means here, stated because it was ambiguous.** The ordinals carry the weighting —
1099	inputs are equally weighted and the tiers differ. If per-input weighting by something else was
1100	intended (sample size, source count, directness), that is a different function and is NOT ruled.
1101	
1102	**Note for the implementer.** `v_best_practice.strength_band` computes a two-value band today; these
1103	are the three `●◐○` bands of `tier-system.md` §5/§8, and no numeric ordinal encoding exists anywhere
1104	in the schema yet. It has to be introduced with the engine rule, not assumed to be present.
1105	
1106	CONDITION: Implementing the band of a `figure_role='derived'` row.
1107	ACTION: floor(mean(ordinal(input bands))), ordinals 3/2/1, inputs equally weighted. Test against the
1108	five rows above; the owner's example is the acceptance case and it falsifies rounding to nearest.
1109	DATE: 2026-09-13 — owner ruling, quoted above.

1429	## Owner ruling 2026-09-17 — PRESENT BOTH notations; never choose between ratio and percentage
1430	
1431	> **"Present both--don't choose between ratio or percentage."**
1432	
1433	**WHAT THIS ANSWERS.** The `DEC` gap raised the same day by the ACTION (2) engine work. A gradient is
1434	written as a ratio (`1:12`, `1:20`) by some sources and as a percentage (`5 %`, `6 %`) by others, and
1435	they are the same physical quantity in two notations. `parse_bound` returns `None` for a ratio by
1436	explicit design, so `compose_value` was building the determination's interval out of the
1437	percentage-stated rows alone — measured on parameter 3: **2 of 7 governing claims**, with five rows
1438	dropped. Migration 086 made that visible in `value_note` instead of silent. The question it left open
1439	was whether the engine may convert, and the answer is that the question was malformed: **the engine
1440	does not pick a notation at all. It presents both.**
1441	
1442	**WHAT IT SETTLES.**
1443	
1444	1. **No notation is dropped.** A governing claim stated as a ratio contributes to the determination on
1445	   the same footing as one stated as a percentage. The 2-of-7 composition was a defect, not a policy.
1446	2. **No notation is privileged.** The determination does not select a "canonical" form and relegate the
1447	   other to a note. Both are carried, and a render surface shows both.
1448	3. **Conversion is for COMPARISON, not for replacement.** The engine must compare across notations to
1449	   apply the most-accommodating rule at all, and `1:20 = 5 %` exactly. That comparison is arithmetic.
1450	   What it must not do is overwrite what a source wrote with the other form.
1451	
1452	**WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, and the limit is arithmetic rather than doctrine.** Some conversions are
1453	exact and some are not: `1:20` is exactly `5 %`, but `1:12` is `8.333…%` and no finite decimal is the
1454	figure the source stated. So a derived notation is **marked as derived**, and where it does not
1455	terminate it is marked as inexact as well. Presenting both does not license presenting a rounded
1456	figure as though a source had written it — that is the 2026-08-19 shape, one column along.
1457	
1458	**A CONSEQUENCE WORTH STATING.** Until this ruling the engine's protection against inventing figures
1459	was to refuse cross-unit composition outright, which cost it five of seven rows on the first cell it
1460	determined. The protection was real and the cost was invisible. Both halves of that stay true and the
1461	remedy is not to relax the refusal but to stop treating two notations of one quantity as two units.
1462	
1463	CONDITION: Any session composing a determination's value from governing claims stated in more than one
1464	notation of the same quantity; any session extending `parse_bound` or `compose_value`.
1465	ACTION: (1) Compose across notations, never within one. (2) Carry every notation the governing set
1466	states, and mark any notation the engine derived rather than read. (3) Mark a derived notation that
1467	does not terminate as inexact; never round it into the position of a stated figure. (4) This is a
1468	ruling about NOTATION of one quantity, not about UNITS: millimetres and degrees remain different
1469	units and the existing refusal to compose across them is untouched. [AMENDED for exact linear units (inches, feet, millimetres, metres) by "Owner rulings 2026-10-29 (second)" below, item 7.]
1470	DATE: 2026-09-17 — owner ruling, quoted above.

1728	## Owner ruling 2026-09-18 — 1979 work is HISTORICAL GROUNDING, not a current standard
1729	
1730	> **"I don't think 1979 work is great for today standards but it's great for historical grounding"**
1731	
1732	Given on contact when batch 18 surfaced Steinfeld, Schroeder and Bishop 1979 (HUD-PDR 397) and was
1733	weighing its tier. Recorded per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0, and it **overrides the tier the ladder would
1734	otherwise have produced on study design alone.**
1735	
1736	**WHAT IT SETTLES, AND IT CUTS AGAINST THE ADMITTING SESSION'S OWN INCLINATION.** On
1737	`governance/tier-system.md` §1 read mechanically, the study is a candidate for
1738	`clinical`/`high_control` → **T1**: the parameter under design was experimentally manipulated (a
1739	purpose-built 40-ft ramp reset from 1:12 to 1:16 to 1:20), the outcome was physiological (pulse
1740	recovery to within ten beats of resting), and n = 124 disabled participants. That is the T1
1741	definition on its face, and it is the reading this session was about to take.
1742	
1743	**The ruling refuses it, and the refusal is about CURRENCY rather than about design quality.** A
1744	determination is a statement about what to build **now**. A 1979 measurement was taken on 1979
1745	wheelchairs, by people trained in 1979 rehabilitation practice, against 1979 expectations of what a
1746	disabled person should have to tolerate — and the anchoring band (T1 / Co-1 / T2 / Co-2) is the band
1747	the guidebook uses to say *this is best practice today*. Historical distance is not a defect in the
1748	study; it is a mismatch between the study and the claim it would be made to anchor.
1749	
1750	**HOW IT IS EXPRESSED IN THE SCHEMA.** `evidence_type='grey'`, `scope='intrinsic'` → **T3**, marker
1751	**○**, which `tier-system.md` §1 glosses as *"Supporting evidence for best-practice claims; rarely
1752	the sole basis"* — precisely "grounding, not standard". The study-design facts are not discarded:
1753	they are recorded in `verification_note` and in the extractions, so a later session can see that a
1754	high-control design was admitted at T3 **by ruling** and not by anyone mistaking its methods.
1755	
1756	**WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY.** It does not retire the source, does not make its findings false, and does
1757	not bar it from a determination's supporting set. It bars it from being the **anchor**. Nor is this
1758	a general rule that old work is weak: it is a ruling about 1979 work being used to state a
1759	present-day building parameter. Where the claim is itself historical — *what did the evidence say
1760	when this code was written* — this source is **primary and first-class**, and that is the use batch
1761	18 makes of it.
1762	
1763	**AND IT LEAVES THE REAL BLOCKER EXACTLY WHERE IT WAS.** Parameter 3 × MOB stays undetermined,
1764	determination gate 1 stays open, and C10 still refuses (GAP-020, GAP-024). This ruling means batch
1765	18 did not move that, and the batch's own pre-registered prior P3 predicted it would not.
1766	
1767	CONDITION: Any session admitting a source published before roughly 1990, or weighing an old but
1768	methodologically strong study for an anchoring tier.
1769	ACTION: (1) Age is a CURRENCY judgement, made separately from study design — do not let a strong
1770	method carry an old source into the anchoring band. (2) Record the design facts anyway, so the T3 is
1771	legible as a ruling rather than as a misreading. (3) Historical-provenance claims are a different

25	## Purpose
26	
27	The Guidebook for Accessible Built Environments equips designers, disabled people, occupational therapists, and policymakers with the questions they need to ask about how to design for accessibility depending on the circumstance.
28

31	When someone knows better, they do better. The guidebook aims to raise the floor of understanding for everyone who touches the built environment.

48	
49	## Doctrinal commitments
50	
51	### 1. Specifications serve questions; questions serve people; people are not uniform
52	
53	Every parameter exposes its within-population variability. Population codes are organizing scaffolding, not a description of any individual within the population. Within-population variation is shown as a first-class data dimension, not buried in narrative caveats. Co-occurring conditions are the norm, not the exception.
54	
55	### 2. Best practice is graded by the evidence hierarchy — code consensus anchors it only at the weak band
56	
57	Best practice is anchored by Tier 1 primary research (OT-prioritized but **not** OT-exclusive — directly-relevant high-control non-OT primary research is admitted at Tier 1, per decision D-E), Co-1 lived experience, Tier 2 synthesis (systematic reviews / meta-analyses and named-organisation evidence-based standards), and Co-2 OT CPGs. Tier 3 lower-control primary clinical evidence is supporting, rarely the sole basis.
58	
59	Tiers 4–6 are a regulatory-baseline stratum: Tier 6 codes are the compliance floor, not the aspiration. **Amended 2026-07-21 (owner directive, Option A; `decisions/DR-2026-07-21-evidence-architecture-option-a-execution.md`):** a best-practice claim derived solely from code consensus — convergence across Tier 4–6 sources — is **not *in error*; it is a weak-band (○) best-practice claim** ("best practice as currently known"), valid only when flagged code-derived with the convergence-not-evidence caveat, never rendered unflagged or above the weak band. (An unflagged or above-weak-band code-consensus best-practice claim *is* still in error.) Convergence is informative (it tells us multiple jurisdictions adopted a value) but is not itself strong evidence: the jurisdictions may be wrong together, or reading from a shared pre-evidence floor that none has updated — which is exactly why the claim sits at the weak band, not why it is excluded.
60	
61	The evidence hierarchy is operative throughout the guidebook; full schema is specified under §Epistemic commitments §Evidence hierarchy below.
62	
63	### 3. Co-1 evidence is co-primary with Tier 1
64	
65	Co-1 evidence — lived experience and participatory design (CRPD Art. 4.3) — is not subordinate to clinical research. The two answer different questions. Where they converge, the convergence is itself evidence. Where they diverge, the divergence is documented and a synthesis approach is specified per parameter (per evidence-state machine in §Epistemic commitments).
66	
67	This is a commitment about evidence types, not about operations. The project's pre-launch solo operational reality is specified separately in §Operational reality.
68	
69	### 4. Design Modes operationalizes the doctrine
70	
71	| Mode | Function | Resolution |
72	|---|---|---|
73	| Universal Mode | Universal Design / Code Compliance | Population-agnostic; fixed values |
74	| Population Mode | Population-Informed Inclusive Design | Ranges; median as default |
75	| Person Mode | Person-Specific Co-Design | The individual's own specific functional needs — their circumstances, capabilities, impairments, and comorbidities. OT co-design resolves the individual case; the design answers may be informed by a related disability population, but that population neither bounds nor defines the person |
76	
77	DAR (Design for Adaptable Readiness) provisions are mandatory at all modes — the structural and electrical infrastructure that allows Person Mode individual adaptation post-construction without major retrofit cost.
78	
79	### 5. Universal design is co-extensive with code compliance — the floor, not an aspiration
80	
81	Inclusive design is the positive aspiration. Universal Mode is the compliance baseline. Best practice exceeds Universal Mode wherever evidence supports.
82	
83	### 6. Questions-led teaching is the project's pedagogical commitment
84	
85	The guidebook organizes around questions readers should ask, not around answers they should adopt. **Questions are first-class data, not annotations.** Navigation modes include a questions-led entry surface (per audit v2 §T-02 / D-01 resolution; B3 specifies the navigation mode).
86	
87	This commitment has both a doctrinal and an epistemic character. As doctrine: the project chooses questions-led structure as its pedagogical stance. As epistemic claim: the project hypothesizes that questions-led resources improve designer outcomes more than prescriptive ones. The doctrinal stance is held; the epistemic claim is tested. See §Epistemic commitments §Questions-led teaching as testable hypothesis.
88	
89	### 7. The guidebook does not substitute for professional judgment
90	
91	Population-level specifications (Universal Mode and Population Mode) are necessary but insufficient. Person-Mode co-design with an occupational therapist resolves the individual case. The guidebook equips professionals to ask better questions; it does not pretend to deliver final answers.

94	
95	## Epistemic commitments
96	
97	The guidebook's epistemic commitments specify *how the project knows what it claims to know* — the evidence types it draws on, the states it permits its claims to occupy, and the limits it declares about its own production.
98	
99	### Evidence hierarchy
100	
101	| Position | Type | Source examples |
102	|---|---|---|
103	| Tier 1 | Primary research with intervention-level or biomechanical control on the parameter under design — OT-prioritized but **not** OT-exclusive (per decision D-E): directly-relevant high-control non-OT primary research (biomechanical / sensory studies on gradients, clearances, acoustic / luminance thresholds) is admitted at Tier 1, not demoted to Tier 3 | OT intervention trials, RCTs; directly-relevant biomechanical / sensory primary studies |
104	| **Co-1** | **Lived experience / participatory design (CRPD Art. 4.3)** — co-primary with Tier 1 | DPO research, peer-reviewed lived-experience literature, named advocacy organizational positions, Co-1-authored academic narratives |
105	| Tier 2 | Community-consensus synthesis above primary studies and below international standards. Two streams: (a) systematic reviews / meta-analyses; (b) named-organisation evidence-based standards (DPO guidelines, professional-body standards) | Cochrane, JBI, narrative SRs; LPA, RNID, HLAA, IDA, Habinteg evidence-based standards |
106	| **Co-2** | **OT professional body CPGs** — parallel to Tier 2 | CAOT, AOTA, RCOT, COTEC, WFOT |
107	| Tier 3 | Lower-control primary clinical research (cross-sectional, observational, qualitative, single-centre) and grey-literature primary research — supporting evidence, rarely the sole basis | Observational / qualitative / single-centre clinical studies; primary grey literature |
108	| Tier 4 | International standards (evidence-based) | ISO 21542, ISO 23599, IEC 60118-4, EN 17210 |
109	| Tier 5 | National beyond-code frameworks | BS 8300-2 Annex G, NL WMO-keuken, RCOTSS-Housing OT |
110	| Tier 6 | Statutory codes | Reference baseline only |
111	
112	Schema encodes both `tier` (1–6) and `evidence_type` (`clinical`, `co1`, `co2`, `sr_meta`, `standard_evidence_based`, `national_framework`, `code`) per Stage 0.5 Decision T-03. Co-primary Co-1 records carry `tier: 1, evidence_type: co1`; Co-2 records carry `tier: 2, evidence_type: co2`. The encoding preserves co-primary parallelism without flattening it into a single tier.
113	
114	### Two orthogonal axes of coverage; directness as a conditioning layer
115	
116	Evidence is located on two orthogonal axes of *coverage*, both always consulted: the **evidence tier** (what kind and strength of evidence) and the **design scale** (Universal / Population / Person). Neither axis determines the other; a Population-scale specification may draw on any evidence tier.
117	
118	**Directness is a conditioning layer over a single population-anchored ladder, not a separate hierarchy per scale.** Evidence is weighted by how well its *grain* matches the *grain of the claim* — bidirectionally, per GRADE's directness principle. An aggregate systematic review is strongest for a population-level claim and down-weighted for a person-specific functional claim; a directly-relevant intervention study is the reverse. The project explicitly rejects a "most-specific-to-least-specific" gradient: directness is grain-matching, not specificity-ranking.
119	
120	**The Design Modes weight the hierarchy asymmetrically by scale.** Universal Mode is a code-floor raised by population-level evidence wherever evidence supports a value above the floor. **The Population scale is where source-ranking does its substantive work** — the evidence hierarchy adjudicates the best-practice value and range there. The Person scale is occupational-therapy resolution of the individual's own functional needs — assessment and clinical-reasoning evidence, not parameter-value-ranking; the population range informs the assessment but does not bound the answer, which may fall outside it (commitment 4). The evidence and design axes therefore remain orthogonal, but under *scale-conditioned weighting*: the axes stay independent, while which evidence carries the most weight is conditioned by the design scale in play. Operational detail is in `governance/evidence-methodology.md` §§1.4, 1.6, 1.7.
121	
122	### Evidence-state machine for best-practice claims
123	
124	Each cell (a parameter under at least one lens; `governance/evidence-architecture.md`) holds one of four states (per Stage 0.5 Decision T-04):
125	
126	| State | Display | Meaning | Validator behavior |
127	|---|---|---|---|
128	| `stated` | normal | Best practice derived from evidence meeting `governance/evidence-methodology.md` §2.2 | Schema-validated; passes evidence-tier-validator |
129	| `provisional` | flagged with confidence | Synthesis based on partial evidence dimension; rich in at least one dimension | Schema-validated; renders with confidence flag |
130	| `pending` | `[BEST-PRACTICE-PENDING]` + gap link | Evidence sparse across all dimensions | Validator requires gap-register entry |
131	| `not_applicable` | "Not applicable" | Parameter has no design implication under this lens | Validator requires explicit rationale |
132	
133	**Silence on evidence-thin populations is not the default.** The Cochrane yardstick distinguishing absence-of-evidence from evidence-of-absence from primary-non-clinical-tier evidence is honored at the cell level (Altman & Bland, 1995, DOI: 10.1136/bmj.311.7003.485; operationalized in Higgins et al., 2024, Cochrane Handbook v6.5, DOI: 10.1002/9781119536604).
134	
135	### Questions-led teaching as testable hypothesis
136	
137	The questions-led pedagogical commitment (Doctrinal commitment 6) is informed by inquiry-based learning, scaffolded questioning in design education, and problem-based learning in professional formation (Schön, 1983, DOI: 10.4324/9781315237473; Hmelo-Silver, 2004, DOI: 10.1023/B:EDPR.0000034022.16470.f3; Royeen, 1995, DOI: 10.5014/ajot.49.4.338). The hypothesis is that questions-led resources improve designer outcomes more than prescriptive ones.
138	
139	The hypothesis is the project's distinctive epistemic claim. It is acknowledged as a claim, not asserted as established. Empirical testing is staged in B6 pilot validation; per Amendment 7 in `workplan/workplan-co0007-v3-amendments.md`, B6 pilot validation pre-launch is solo-author cross-checking against committed mission language, which is weaker rigor than external testing would provide. This methodological limit is declared, not papered over.
140	
141	### Treatment of evidence convergence and divergence
142	
143	Where Tier 1 clinical evidence and Co-1 lived experience converge on a parameter, the convergence is documented as strengthening the claim — neither dimension subsumes the other.
144	
145	Where they diverge, the divergence is itself evidence about how the parameter operates differently in clinical assessment versus lived use. The synthesis specifies which dimension governs the best-practice claim and on what reasoning, with the divergence visible to the reader. A synthesis that suppresses divergence is in error.
146	
147	### Citation discipline
148	
149	- Every Part-4 specification carries an evidence marker: ● (confirmed), ◐ (policy/standards only) or ○ (grey, thin, or unverified because the source could not be retrieved), the band assigned per `governance/tier-system.md` §5/§8; a determination carries the band `assess_cell` computes (`specifications.marker`). Unmarked = error.
150	- Quantified outcome claims require DOI + page/table reference, or failing that, direct URL to source. Unverified claims carry `[UNVERIFIED-QUANT]` flag.
151	- Two failed independent searches → CLOSED-DELETED disposition for unverifiable values; do not accumulate unresolvable UNVERIFIED flags.
152	- Source authenticity: confirmed real before citation. "I don't know" governs over invention.
153

155	
156	## Methodological boundaries
157	
158	The guidebook specifies for **formal new construction and planned retrofit**. Informal settlement housing is out of specification scope (per project-standards 2026-04-07 00:44, recorded as the project's most significant scope-shaped exclusion). The formal/informal city divide is the meta-barrier to global accessible housing; the guidebook acknowledges this as the highest-priority research and policy gap in its domain.
159	
160	The guidebook is **not a substitute for professional judgment**. Population-level specifications (Universal Mode and Population Mode) are necessary but insufficient. Person-Mode co-design with an occupational therapist resolves the individual case.
161	
162	The guidebook is **not a legal authority**. It does not replace jurisdictional code compliance (which is Tier 6 — the floor). Where evidence-based best practice exceeds code, the guidebook specifies the evidence-based value and notes the code value as the regulatory minimum.
163	
164	The guidebook does **not pursue universal jurisdictional adoption** as its primary trajectory; it pursues equipping practitioners to make informed decisions in any jurisdiction. Trajectory positioning toward formal adoption is an A11 decision.
165	
166	The guidebook is a **pre-launch single-author synthesis** drawing on published Co-1 evidence, Tier 1–6 literature, and the author's reading and judgment. Methodological integrity rests on honest evidence engagement and transparent declaration of limits — not on a fictional collaborative production structure.
167	
168	---
169	
170	## Operational reality
171	
172	The project is currently pre-launch and authored by a single person. There are no Co-1 collaborator panels, no DPO partnerships, no recruitment thread, and no compensation infrastructure. Co-1 *evidence* is engaged through the published corpus only — peer-reviewed lived-experience literature, confirmed Co-1 advocacy positions from named organizations, and Co-1-authored academic narratives.
173	
174	This is **evidence-level engagement** with Co-1, not **participation-level engagement**. CRPD Art. 4.3 is honored in partial form: the corpus engaged was itself produced through participatory processes, and the synthesis here treats that corpus as co-primary with Tier 1. Direct participation in the synthesis is not happening pre-launch. This is the methodological limit, declared.
175	
176	If the project launches and resources permit, the form of collaboration with disabled people becomes a co-design question — to be answered with disabled people, not for them. Specifying that form pre-launch, in the absence of participants, would reproduce the substantive problem CRPD Art. 4.3 exists to address.
177	
178	A5 (per `workplan/workplan-co0007-v3-amendments.md` Amendment 7) produces a design specification for the post-launch collaborative form: a how-it-would-work document that activates if and when conditions allow. This may never activate. **Solo-only-permanent is a possible end-state for the project.** The methodology must hold integrity in that case as well as in the launched-with-collaboration case.
179	
180	The mission's claim to honor CRPD Art. 4.3 is calibrated honestly: partial pre-launch (corpus engagement); full only if launched-and-resourced; possibly never full.

184	## Test against which all downstream decisions are evaluated
185	
186	Every methodological, architectural, and editorial decision in the project must be evaluated against this mission. The test:
187	
188	1. Does this decision help readers ask better questions about how to design for accessibility?
189	2. Does it acknowledge non-uniformity — within-population variability and individual specificity?
190	3. Does it grade best practice by the evidence hierarchy — treating code consensus as the weak (○) band, flagged, rather than as full strength or as excluded?
191	4. Does it surface where Co-1 evidence governs, where Tier 1 clinical evidence governs, where they converge, and where they diverge?
192	5. Does it respect the operational reality on Co-1 (pre-launch solo synthesis from published corpus) and document the partial-honoring limit honestly?
193	6. Does it leave professional judgment to the reader rather than substitute for it?
194	7. Is the underlying data verifiable (clean data) and the methodology declared (transparent methodology)?
195	8. Does it align with the audience-priority structure in `governance/audience-priority.md` — primary needs governing direct content, secondary needs governing cross-references and supplements?
196	
197	Decisions that fail this test must be revised, document a justified exception, or trigger a mission revision.

281	### 1.2 Selection criteria
282	
283	The 24 jurisdictions were selected to satisfy four coverage criteria:
284	
285	1. **Geographic diversity** — all inhabited continents represented; Global South ≥8 jurisdictions
286	2. **Regulatory model diversity** — prescriptive codes (FR, SG), performance-based codes (AU, NZ), hybrid (UK, US), minimal/emerging (BD, KE, NG)

291

298	## 2. Jurisdiction and evidence tier relationship
299	
300	### 2.1 Codes are Tier 6
301	
302	Per Core Doctrine: "Codes are Tier 6: the compliance floor, not the aspiration." This means:
303	
304	- A code value establishes what the minimum legal standard is in that jurisdiction
305	- A code value does NOT establish best practice
306	- Code consensus (many jurisdictions agreeing on the same value) is stronger than a single code but weaker than Tier 4–5 standards or Tier 1–3 clinical evidence
307	- A BPC best_practice_synthesis derived solely from code consensus is a weak-band (○) flagged "best practice as currently known" claim — not full strength, not excluded (project-standards L20, amended 2026-07-21 Option A)
308	
309	### 2.2 Standards are Tier 4–5
310	
311	International standards (ISO, IEC, EN) with an evidence basis are Tier 4. National beyond-code frameworks (BS 8300-2 Annex G, SINTEF guidelines, NEN/NL WMO-keuken) are Tier 5. Both outrank codes but are below clinical evidence and Co-1/Co-2.
312	
313	### 2.3 Per-jurisdiction tier coverage
314

319	| `status` | SEARCHED, THIN, NO-DATA, NOT-RUN | Research status for this jurisdiction on this parameter |
320	| `co1_attempted` | bool | Whether Co-1 evidence was searched for this jurisdiction |
321	| `tier5_attempted` | bool | Whether Tier 5 (beyond-code framework) evidence was searched |
322	| `tier6_attempted` | bool | Whether Tier 6 (code) evidence was searched |
323	
324	A BPC entry is PROVISIONAL until the Co-1 pass covers ≥9 languages.

417	# Audience Priority
418	**Status:** CANONICAL — locked at iter 4 cross-test pass (2026-04-26 05:29)
419	**Created:** 2026-04-26 03:55 UTC; iter 2 deltas 2026-04-26 04:05 UTC
420	**Iteration plan:** `workplan/a1-a2-iteration-plan.md`

420	**Iteration plan:** `workplan/a1-a2-iteration-plan.md`
421	**Operative frame:** Pre-launch solo authorship; partial CRPD Art. 4.3 honoring at evidence level
422	**Companion deliverable:** `governance/mission-and-epistemics.md` (canonical-track iter 1; iter 4 acceptance produces canonical lock for both)
423	
424	---
425	
426	## Operational role of this document
427	
428	This document is the test-target for `governance/mission-and-epistemics.md` §Test item 8: *"Does it align with the audience-priority structure in `governance/audience-priority.md` — primary needs governing direct content, secondary needs governing cross-references and supplements?"*
429	
430	That status carries weight: every downstream content choice in the guidebook is checked against this document. The audience-priority structure must therefore be robust enough to bear the test. Where iter 1's rules do not cover a content choice cleanly, iter 2 either tightens them or routes the choice to A6 (evidence methodology) / A12 (decision-capture protocol) for resolution by domain-specific rule rather than audience-priority extension.
431	
432	`governance/mission-PROVISIONAL.md` is superseded as of iter 4 canonical lock (2026-04-26 05:29). This file and `governance/mission-and-epistemics.md` are now the operative governance pair.
433	
434	---
435	
436	## Why audience priority is an operational question
437	
438	Audience priority answers a recurring question in content production: *when reading needs diverge, whose needs govern?* It is not a worth-judgment about who matters more. It is an operational rule that resolves choices about content layering, navigation entry, terseness vs framing, and cross-reference structure. Without an audience-priority rule, every such choice would be made ad hoc and the guidebook would drift toward whichever audience the author imagines most clearly while drafting any given passage. With the rule, choices are accountable.
439	
440	The four named audiences — designers, disabled people, occupational therapists, policymakers — are confirmed in mission-PROVISIONAL §Audiences and carried forward in `governance/mission-and-epistemics.md` §Purpose and §Audience commitments. This document specifies their operational priority and the use-patterns within each.
441	
442	**Ordering convention.** Within the primary class, designers and disabled people are presented in that sequence; within the secondary class, OTs and policymakers are presented in that sequence. The within-class ordering is alphabetical-within-role (architect/designer A precedes disabled-person D; occupational-therapist O precedes policymaker P) and is **not** a priority claim within its class. Both members of a class are equally primary or equally secondary. The primary-vs-secondary distinction is the priority claim; within-class ordering is presentation only. Mission-and-epistemics §Audience commitments documents the parallel convention for the Purpose statement.
443	
444	---
445	
446	## Primary audiences
447	
448	**Primary status is granted to the audiences at the production-use endpoints of the built environment: those who produce environments and those who use them.**
449	
450	### Designers (architects, interior designers)
451	
452	Designers produce environments. Decisions made at programming, schematic design, design development, and construction documentation determine what the built environment is. The guidebook's most direct mechanism of effect on accessibility is changing those decisions.
453	
454	**Use-patterns:**
455	
456	| Pattern | Reader state | Content need |
457	|---|---|---|
458	| Information-finding | Looking up a specific value for a specific parameter for a specific population at a specific design stage | Tabulated, precise, retrievable; minimal framing in the immediate cell; cross-references to fuller treatment |
459	| Decision-frame | Facing a population-implicating design decision; wants to think through considerations | Narrative around the spec data; questions to ask; alternatives surfaced; trade-offs named |
460	
461	These are different reading modes engaging the same underlying data. Content production must serve both modes — typically by layering (table + surrounding prose) rather than by producing two parallel artifacts.
462	
463	### Disabled people (themselves)
464	
465	Disabled people use environments. Their lived experience tests whether what gets built actually serves them. The guidebook's claim to evidence-based best practice is empty if it is not legible and accountable to the people whose needs it claims to specify.
466	
467	**Use-patterns:**
468	
469	| Pattern | Reader state | Content need |
470	|---|---|---|
471	| Information-finding | What should I expect / ask for / advocate for in a built environment shaped around my needs? What does my condition imply for specific design parameters? | Accessible specs in plain language; cross-references to advocacy use; precise enough to cite when asking for change |
472	| Representation-checking | Is my experience acknowledged? Is within-population variability honored, or am I subsumed under a generic label? | Narrative framing surfacing variability; explicit acknowledgment that population codes are organizing scaffolding, not descriptions of any individual; visible Co-1 evidence basis |
473	| Advocacy-brief *(added per unification-DR item G5, ACCEPTED 2026-07-13; available by extension to carers and DPO staff)* | What can I cite when asking for better than the legal minimum? | The code-vs-evidence delta rendered honestly (no delta asserted before value extraction supports it); rights framing (CRPD-linked); citable evidence strength with instrument-status caveats — a wrongly-cited "legal minimum" hands the other side a rebuttal |
474	
475	Representation-checking is unusual among reading modes: the reader is **testing** the document, not just reading it. The document must hold up under that test. A document that fails representation-checking is failing in its core commitment, not merely in style.
476	
477	---
478	
479	## Secondary audiences
480	
481	**Secondary status is granted to audiences whose work shapes the conditions of others' production or use: intermediaries between code, individual assessment, and the built environment.**
482	
483	### Occupational therapists
484	
485	OTs operate at the individual side of the built environment — assessing how a specific person engages a specific environment, intervening through co-design at Tier 2. They have established clinical training; the guidebook supplements rather than primarily teaches them.
486	
487	**Use-patterns:**
488	
489	| Pattern | Reader state | Content need |
490	|---|---|---|
491	| Clinical-collaboration | Co-designing a built-environment intervention with a client; bringing population-level specifications into individual-specific assessment | Population-Mode ranges legible alongside the median, with the Person-Mode resolution path identified |
492	| Specialist-handoff | Communicating an OT assessment finding to a non-OT designer or builder; using the guidebook as common-ground language | Population codes and parameter labels stable enough to cite; cross-references to the matching item specification |
493	
494	### Policymakers
495	
496	Policymakers shape codes and policy. The guidebook is evidence-grounded best practice that informs rule-making — it is not itself a code and does not aim to become one. Tier 6 codes are the floor; the guidebook specifies the evidence-based aspiration.
497	
498	**Use-patterns:**
499	
500	| Pattern | Reader state | Content need |
501	|---|---|---|
502	| Jurisdiction-comparison | What do other jurisdictions do for this provision? Why? | The 24/46/49 jurisdiction structure (per A8) navigable; comparable provisions surfaced |
503	| Rationale | What is the evidence basis for this best-practice value? | Citation chain visible; tier hierarchy applied; gap between code value and evidence-based value made explicit |
504	
505	---
506	
507	## Audiences by extension
508	
509	The guidebook does not produce dedicated content for the following readers, but its structure makes it usable by them through one of the four core audience modes:
510	
511	- **Students** (architecture, occupational therapy, disability studies) — typically read in designer-decision-frame mode or OT-clinical-collaboration mode
512	- **Researchers** — typically read in policymaker-rationale mode
513	- **Facility managers / building owners** — typically read in designer-information-finding mode
514	- **Builders, contractors, inspectors** — typically read in designer-information-finding mode for specific items
515	
516	These uses are accommodated by extension. They do not constrain content choices independently. If an extension-by-use need cannot be served by any of the four primary/secondary use-pattern paths, that is a structural gap to log, not a tertiary-audience target to add.
517	
518	---
519	
520	## Conflict-resolution rules
521	
522	### Within-primary conflicts
523	
524	When designer-information-finding needs and disabled-person-representation-checking needs apply to the same content cell:
525	
526	1. **Default: layer both.** Spec table for lookup precision; framing prose surrounding the table for representation acknowledgment. Most cells admit both.
527	2. **Where layering is impossible** (e.g., a single sentence in a tight prose passage): representation acknowledgment governs framing language; numeric/parameter precision governs measurement text. The two coexist within the sentence.
528	3. **Where the representation-check would return a "this is wrong about my experience" verdict** for a defensible disabled reader: that is a content failure overriding designer convenience. Re-draft the cell.
529	
530	**Pre-launch methodological note.** Per `governance/mission-and-epistemics.md` §Operational reality and §Epistemic commitments §Questions-led teaching as testable hypothesis, B6 pilot validation pre-launch is solo-author cross-checking — weaker rigor than external testing would provide. Representation-checking, performed by disabled readers in actual use of the document, is therefore the principal *audience-side* rigor available in the pre-launch state. The doctrinal weight of representation-checking as a use-pattern is correspondingly elevated: a content failure on representation-check is not a rigor problem the project has external scaffolding to catch through other channels. This may shift post-launch if external Co-1 review becomes available.
531	
532	### Within-secondary conflicts
533	
534	When OT-clinical-collaboration and policymaker-rationale needs apply to the same content cell:
535	
536	1. Default: serve clinical-collaboration in the primary content body; serve rationale in cross-references to evidence base, jurisdiction matrix, and bibliography.
537	2. Where conflict cannot be resolved by structural placement, primary audiences govern any framing decision; secondary audiences accept the resulting structure.
538	
539	### Primary vs secondary conflicts
540	
541	1. Primary's needs govern direct content placement, primary navigation paths, and the language of doctrinal commitments.
542	2. Secondary's needs govern cross-reference structure, appendices, jurisdiction matrices, evidence-tier listings, and supplementary materials.
543	3. A secondary-audience need that would require restructuring primary content paths is logged as a gap, not absorbed.
544	
545	### Within-audience use-pattern conflicts
546	
547	When information-finding and decision-frame patterns apply to the same designer reader at the same moment, or information-finding and representation-checking apply to the same disabled-person reader:
548	
549	1. **Entry path governs.** A reader entering through a specification page is in information-finding mode; a reader entering through a Part introduction or doctrinal commitment is in decision-frame or representation-checking mode.
550	2. **Where entry path is ambiguous, default to the more demanding pattern**: representation-checking for disabled people, decision-frame for designers. The more demanding pattern produces content that also serves the simpler pattern; the reverse is not true.
551	
552	---
553	
554	## What this means for content production
555	
556	| Content type | Audience priority signal | Content production rule |
557	|---|---|---|
558	| Item specifications | Designer information-finding + disabled-person information-finding | Tabulated lookup-friendly parameter data; framing prose surrounding; population codes navigable |
559	| Population sections | Disabled-person representation-checking | Narrative-led; within-population variability surfaced; co-occurrence as norm; population code as scaffold not description |
560	| Conflict-resolution sections (Parts 3, 5, 7) | Designer decision-frame + OT clinical-collaboration | Decision-framework structured; questions to ask; resolution paths identified; not prescriptive answers |
561	| Front matter and Part introductions | Designer decision-frame + disabled-person representation-checking | Questions-led teaching mode; doctrinal commitments visible; mission language audible |
562	| Appendices and bibliographies | Policymaker rationale + OT specialist-handoff | Citation chains; jurisdiction matrices; tier-hierarchy listings; evidence basis retrievable |
563	| Cross-references | All audiences | Stable; navigable both directions; pattern consistent across Volumes I and II |

1	# Pipeline operations — what each one consumes, produces, and logs
2	
3	**Status:** PROPOSED · **Date:** 2026-08-02 · **Scope:** definitional
4	
5	This document exists because **"mining" in this project means at least two different
6	operations with different inputs, different outputs, and different tables** — and the bare word
7	has been used for both. Migration 040 named a column `citation_mining_status` rather than
8	`mining_status` for exactly this reason.
9	
10	The rule this document establishes:
11	
12	> **No column, check, or skill may use "mining" unqualified.** Name the operation.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## 1. The five operations
17	
18	The single most useful distinction: **discovery produces _sources_, extraction produces _values_,
19	synthesis produces _statements_.** Confusing them is what lets a source be "processed" in one sense
20	and untouched in another.
21	
22	| # | Operation | Consumes | Produces | Output table | Log of the act |
23	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
24	| 1 | **Search execution** | a query × index × language × jurisdiction | screened results | `search_candidates` | `search_executions` |
25	| 2 | **Citation mining** *(anchor-driven discovery)* | one confirmed source, as an anchor | further candidate **sources** | `search_candidates` / new `evidence_sources` | `citation_mining` (per slug × local ref) + `evidence_sources.citation_mining_status` |
26	| 3 | **Gap-driven mining** *(gap-driven discovery)* | one open row in `gaps` | further candidate **sources** | `search_candidates` | `gap_mining` |
27	| 4 | **Data extraction** *(value capture)* | one source we hold | **values**, with locator and lens grain, keyed on the parameter (`db.py add-extraction`) | `source_value_extractions`, `spec_value_probes`, `jurisdictional_values`, `economics_entries` | the extraction rows, each carrying its session |
28	| 5 | **Synthesis** | extracted values across sources for one (parameter × lens) | a **best-practice statement** with an evidence marker | `specifications` + `convergence_assessment` | `specifications.derivation_sha`, attestations |
29	
30	*Rows 4 and 5 read `(item × population)` until 2026-09-10. Migrations 071 and 073 re-keyed both
31	tables onto `parameter_id` and the four lens columns (owner 2026-08-26 and 2026-08-28); the item
32	layer was emptied 2026-09-01 and `items` is a Part-4 render rollup derived from specifications.*
33	
34	Adjudication (does this source qualify for admission, at which tier) is not a sixth operation —
35	it is the gate between 1–3 and 4, recorded on the source itself
36	(`verification_status`, `tier`, `search_candidates.disposition`).
37	
38	---
39	
40	## 2. The distinctions that keep being lost
41	
42	**Citation mining reads a source's _bibliography_. Data extraction reads its _content_.**
43	A source can be fully mined and hold no captured value, or hold captured values and never have
44	been mined. They are independent axes, which is why migration 040 gave `evidence_sources` two
45	separate status columns rather than one "processed" flag.
46	
47	**Citation mining is source-scoped; gap-driven mining is gap-scoped.** That is why
48	`citation_mining_status` can live on `evidence_sources` and a gap-mining status cannot. It is
49	also why `citation_mining`'s primary key is `(slug, local_ref_id)` — one source is mined *for a
50	given slug*, and a source may serve up to 7 slugs.
51	
52	**Discovery does not admit.** Producing a candidate is not admitting a source. R10 governs the
53	boundary: no re-retrieval, no admission.
54	
55	**Extraction is not synthesis.** Capturing "RT60 ≤ 0.6 s, BB93 §1.2, classrooms" is extraction.
56	Deciding what the best practice *is* across sources, populations and jurisdictions is synthesis,
57	and only synthesis is gated to Opus-class authorship (PI rule #2, DR-2026-06-10).
58	
59	---
60	
61	## 3. Where each operation stands today
62	
63	Measured 2026-08-02 and left at that vintage on purpose — every row below predates the
64	2026-08-12 evidence-stage clearance, after which `search_executions`, `evidence_sources`,
65	`gaps`, `source_value_extractions` and `specifications` are all **0 rows**. Derive current
66	numbers rather than trusting these; a row here is a record of the 08-02 state, not a claim
67	about today.
68	
69	| Operation | State |
70	|---|---|
71	| Search execution | `search_executions` 84 rows, 3 days of activity; 39 admissions logged against 863 sources |
72	| Citation mining | 100 sources mined, 67 deferred, **696 pending**. Tier 1–2, where R2 obliges the work: **134 pending, 23 deferred, 34 mined of 191** |
73	| Gap-driven mining | `gap_mining` **0 rows** — the table exists and has never been written to; 50 gaps OPEN |
74	| Data extraction | **11 of 863** sources have a joinable capture row; 852 pending |
75	| Synthesis | `specifications` 15 rows of a 93 × 23 grid |
76	
77	---
78	
79	## 4. The logging rule, and its unresolved tension
80	
81	Each operation must leave a row saying it happened, so that "not done" and "done, nothing found"
82	are distinguishable states rather than the same absence. Migration 040 closed that gap for
83	operations 2 and 4 at source grain.
84	
85	**A status column without a biconditional check is an assertion nobody verifies.** The first
86	backfill of `citation_mining_status` resolved rows by `global_ref_id` alone — NULL in 146 of 183
87	rows — and left 80 sources reading `pending` while holding a non-deferred mining row. The mining
88	status had no check, so nothing contradicted it; it has one now (`C08`). Any future status column
89	ships with its check or it does not ship.
90	
91	**Unresolved (⚑8 in the current plan):** under migrations-only, a log row is authored by the same
92	session whose compliance it attests, at commit time, with self-reported timestamps. R8's
93	append-only check catches deletion, not omission — and omission is precisely what produced 39
94	logged admissions against 863 sources. There are three possible homes and no fourth: migrations
95	(confessional, status quo), job-owned direct writers (one DR per table under DR-2026-05-28 §3), or
96	a new hook-owned class. Until that is decided, "mandatory logging" means "self-reported logging".
97	
98	---
99	
100	## 5. Prose and values
101	
102	A **state** is a coded value: `pending`, `deferred`, `no-full-text`. It goes in a constrained
103	column so it can be counted, joined and checked.
104	
105	**Extracted content may be prose** — a verbatim claim, a quoted clause — provided it sits in a
106	dedicated table with the pointers that make it traceable, alongside the typed value it
107	accompanies. `source_value_extractions` is the model: `claimed_value` and `claimed_unit` are
108	typed, `claim_text` is the verbatim quote, `source_section` and the 16 `loc_*` columns are the
109	locator, and `ref_id`, `slug`, `parameter_id`, the four lens columns and `promoted_to_rdc_id`
110	carry the trace. *(This named `population_code` until 2026-09-10; migration 073 retired it in
111	favour of the four lens columns, under the 2026-08-28 owner ruling.)*
112	
113	What is forbidden is a **state written as prose in a value column**. This is not hypothetical:
114	four rows held `[author surname pending …]` in `first_author_last`, and because the string was
115	non-empty the blocking `C03` check counted them as having an author. A missing author passed a
116	gate by wearing a value's clothes. Check `C07` now forbids the pattern.
117

88	### 2.1 Key relationships
89	
90	**ENT-02 → ENT-03 → ENT-01 (evidence flow):** Sources feed into BPC entries. BPC synthesis produces specifications. This is the primary content pipeline. The `bpc_source_slug` field on Specification already encodes this. The `used_in_slugs` field on Evidence Source encodes the inverse.
91	
92	**ENT-01 → ENT-08 (specification → item):** Many specifications roll up into one item. The `item_code` field on Specification already encodes this. Item is the Part 4 organizing unit.

94	**ENT-08 → ENT-17 (item → room/space):** Items are placed in rooms via matrices (Parts 6/7). This is an N:N relationship — an item appears in multiple room types, and a room type includes many items.

98	### 4.5 Genealogy — counting roots, not documents
99	
100	Directness conditions how much a source's *claim* weighs. Genealogy conditions how much a value's *apparent agreement* weighs. It gives the project's central adjudication — best practice versus consensus — a computable form. `[H1 — DR-2026-07-13-value-genealogy-and-derivation-handshake, ratified 2026-07-13]`
101	
102	The doctrine in one line: **precedent counts documents; evidence counts roots.** Twenty-four jurisdictions specifying the same figure is one fact about transmission, not twenty-four facts about disabled people. This is the §2 convergence-not-evidence rule pushed one level down — from *which stratum is agreeing?* to *how many independent measurements are they all agreeing about?* The corridor case is the worked proof (§8.1; `references/methodology/value-genealogy-worked-example-corridor-width.md`): 1500mm turning "circles" across 24 jurisdictions trace to a single 1970s anthropometric root whose own authors record it as needing updating; the 1800mm passing consensus has no traceable root anywhere in the corpus; 2440/2400mm has two independent roots (ASL proxemics, Co-1; swept-path anthropometry, T3) plus one untraced regulatory convergence.
103	
104	**Storage.** Each extracted value on `source_value_extractions` carries `root_id`, `root_type` (`measurement_primary` / `participatory_finding` / `committee_assertion` / `derived_calculation` / `untraced`), `root_ref_id`, `echo_of`, `measurement_paradigm`, `device_class`, `root_population_note`, `file_anchor`, `root_classification_basis`, `contested`. The discriminator is the view `v_value_independence`: independent roots **per parameter**, counting DISTINCT roots and excluding `committee_assertion`. *(Swept 2026-09-10 with migration 073, which names this file as a prose caller of that view. The sentence read "per (parameter, population)"; the population half went with migration 071, which took `population_code` out of the view's grain, and 073 re-derived the view a second time onto `parameter_id`. It groups by `parameter_id` alone — the lens is the determination's, not the root count's.)*
105	
106	**Three anti-gaming disciplines, structural rather than editorial.** (a) *Root registry* — a `root_id` must resolve either to a `root_ref_id` in `evidence_sources` or to a registered external-root stub, so two extractors cannot mint two ids for one root and double the count. (b) *Untraced rows carry NULL `root_id` and are excluded from the count* — untraceability can never out-score a traced chain. (c) *`root_classification_basis` + `contested`* — the root-versus-echo judgment is recordably disputable, not free-text folklore.
107	
108	**AMENDED** 2026-10-14 in the first alternative of discipline (a), by `references/project-standards.md`: "the rule becomes that `source_value_extractions.root_id` references `external_root_registry` and nothing else". A `root_id` names a registered external root; a root held in `evidence_sources` is named by `root_ref_id`. The rest of this paragraph stands. See the ledger entry "Recording 2026-10-14, third part".
109	
110	**The six adjudication tests — four encoded, two doctrinal.** Root, Independence, Paradigm-commensurability and Fit-population map onto the fields above. *Currency* rides the existing supersession machinery (`evidence_sources.superseded_by_ref_id` + DR-2026-05-24) rather than duplicating it. *Interest* — who convened the consensus? — is recorded in `root_classification_basis` notes: doctrinal, not a column, until a real vocabulary for convening-interest emerges from use. Cross-paradigm and cross-device-class applications are recorded as **derivations, never identities**: a static turning circle cannot corroborate a swept-path envelope (most real turns are asymmetric spin turns; scooters have no pivot at all), and a figure a source declares manual-wheelchair-only does not silently become a power-chair figure.
111	
112	`[BUILD STATE 2026-08-15 — DATED, AND THE FIGURE HAS MOVED: the fields, the external-root registry and v_value_independence exist in the canonical DB; source_value_extractions held 0 rows ON THAT DATE and holds neither 0 nor any number this sentence may state (rule 7a). Count it, never quote it: `python3 -c "import sqlite3;print(sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True).execute('select count(*) from source_value_extractions').fetchone()[0])"`. The clause below is conditioned on that count being zero and stops applying the moment it is not. Genealogy is an available discriminator with nothing yet to discriminate — the extraction pass is Phase-E work. No determination may cite root-independence until rows exist, and an empty view returning no roots is not a finding of no independence: it is the Altman & Bland distinction (§9) applied to this table.]`
